# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

### HTTP API (entry points)
| Route | File:line | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | `Controller.py:51-53` | health check |
| `POST /recurrentTransactions` | `Controller.py:55-67` | recurring txn detection |

| `clean_input_df` | `:6-12` |
| `sep_by_` (split on `/`) | `:14-15` |
| `sep_by_dash` (`-`) | `:17-18` |
| `sep_by_wave` (`~`) | `:20-21` |
| `sep_by_star` (`*`) | `:23-24` |
| `sep_by_comma` (`,`) | `:26-27` |
| `sep_by_colon` (`:`) | `:29-30` |
| `sep_by_under` (`_`) | `:32-33` |
| `sep_by_brckt` / `sep_by_right_brckt` / `sep_by_square_brckt` / `sep_by_square_right_brckt` | `:35-45` |

## 4. Fixtures / test corpora and how tests are run

**There are none.** Verified exhaustively:

- `git ls-files` → 54 files, all `.py` + `Dockerfile` + `.gitignore`; single commit `047782b import codebase`; only branch `main`.
- No file or directory anywhere in the repo matching `*test*`, `*fixture*`, `*.json`, `*.csv`, `*.xls*`, `*.yml`, `*.yaml`, `*.cfg`, `*.ini`, `*.toml`, `*.md` (search excluded `.git`).
- No `tests/`, no `conftest.py`, no `pytest.ini`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`, no `.github/`, no CI config, no README, no sample payloads.

## Root cause

I traced the corpus to **AU Small Finance Bank** (`bank = AU_SMALL_FINANCE_BANK`). Replaying the quoted narration through all 35 bank paths, AU is the only one that reproduces all five fingerprints — notably F-2's exact `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → `Micr Clg`, and F-4's bare reference number *while the neighbouring layout still resolves*. AU is also the thinnest script in the repo (102 lines, no entry in `BankRegexConstants.py`), so each finding is a missing narration form rather than a broken rule.

| # | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| F-1 | AU had no rule for a cheque number arriving in the reference/note column — 10+ other banks do (`YES.py:52`, `Axis.py:58`…). Bare-number notes fell through to `default="TRANSFER"`. | `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:53` — bare-number note + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`, placed **last** so every narration rule keeps precedence and only rows that already defaulted to `TRANSFER` can move. |
| F-2 | `^CHQ PAID-` took dash segment 1 unconditionally; with the clearing tag present that segment *is* `MICR CLG`. | `:91` — dedicated `CHQ_CLG_AU` extraction for the tag layout, ahead of the positional rule. Same one-line hole existed in `Canara.py:165`, closed identically (Canara already had the precedent for `Home Clearing`). |
| F-3 | Only `NEFT [CD][Rr]-` and `Received from … A/C … NEFT` were described; other inbound layouts matched nothing → `default=""`. | `:115-118` — fallbacks for name-after-reference/IFSC, `Received from …`, direction tag, and name-after-scheme. |
| F-4 | `IMPS-` always took dash segment 2; on the `IMPS-<name>-<ref>` layout that segment is the reference. | `:113` — re-derives the sender when the extracted value is a bare number. |
| F-5 | Verification vocabulary was three literals, and `amount.eq(1)` only. | `:20` — canonical `BANK_VER` vocabulary (shared with HDFC/Axis/BOM) at `amount.between(0,2)`. |

The two name-repair passes are **guarded by the wrong value they repair** (all-digits, or empty) and scoped to remittance categories, so a name that already resolves can't be overwritten — `AUTO_PAYMENT`'s numeric mandate reference is explicitly left alone.

## Verification

- **Diff against pre-change behaviour**: 73 narrations × 32 banks × 2 account types. Exactly 18 rows move — 15 AU + 3 Canara — and every one is a listed finding. All ordinary traffic holds, including the low-value rows that guard the widened verification rule (₹1 UPI credit, ₹1 NEFT credit, ₹1 interest, ₹1/₹1.5 charges, ₹2 cash deposit).
- **End-to-end** through `POST /categorizeTransaction` → HTTP 200 with correct categories and names. (The `transactionDate` warning and the `- Cheque` suffix in `pfmSimpleDescription` are pre-existing and byte-identical before/after — untouched.)
- **Payload robustness**: AU never read `remark` before, so I handled the column being absent, numeric, or null, plus single-row and empty frames.
- **Regression cover**: `categorizationapp/tests/test_rc214_categorization.py` — 37 cases, one per finding plus the baseline-stable neighbours. `pytest categorizationapp/tests` → 37 passed, offline and deterministic.

One thing I deliberately did **not** change: `IMPS Received from …` credits are categorised `TRANSFER` rather than `IMPS` in AU (the name resolves correctly). It's a real gap, but F-4 states the category on those rows is right, so it's outside this build's acceptance and worth a separate ticket.
